transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 mins
Attendees: Jamie Park / Marisol Chen / Omar Reyes (Redwood) — Ravi Patil / Elsa Moreno / Dana Price / Kevin Li (Crestline)

Summary:
Quick scoping session to align POC milestones, clarify success criteria (latency & cost targets, data isolation), finalize access plan (VPC, service accounts, SSO) and agree mid-point review + exec readout cadence. Action items captured.

Topics:
- Kickoff and access setup timeline
- Workload sizing and benchmark definition (token distribution, QPS, sequence lengths)
- Mid-point (2 week) technical review and 4-week exec readout
- Security questions: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, data retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — good morning, afternoon, whatever — I'm Jamie from Redwood, AE for this deal. Quick around the table?
[00:10] Ravi Patil: Hi this is Ravi, I'm head of data at Crestline — we'll run the POC and own metrics.
[00:15] Elsa Moreno: Elsa, platform eng, I'll handle VPC/networking and infra access.
[00:18] Dana Price: Dana here, CTO — I'll be in for exec readouts and the business criteria.
[00:22] Kevin Li: Kevin, security architect. Soc2 questions probably for later.
[00:26] Marisol Chen: Marisol, Solutions Eng at Redwood — I'll run the benchmarks and help tune.
[00:30] Omar Reyes: Omar from CS, I'll help with pilot ops and logistics.

[01:02] Jamie Park: Great. Goal for today is to agree scope: what are the success criteria, how we'll size the workload, and what exact milestones get us to an exec readout. Also we want to confirm access so Marisol can run the first benchmark within the week.
[01:18] Ravi Patil: For success, we have three buckets: latency at p95 under 400ms for typical chat flows, cost per 1k tokens under our internal target — which I'll share — and compatibility with our data governance, meaning no egress of PII and ability to keep logs in our KMS.
[01:36] Marisol Chen: That helps. When you say "chat flows" can you give an example sequence length distribution? Are we talking 32 tokens prompts and 256 tokens responses or heavier?
[01:44] Ravi Patil: Mix. Roughly 60% short Q&A (15-60 tokens), 30% medium (100-250 tokens), and 10% long (400-1200 tokens) — some reranking on the back end for document search.

[02:10] Elsa Moreno: On infra, we prefer a private deployment model — ideally VPC peering with your hosted control plane, but we're open to dedicated capacity if the security overhead is lower. We need clear network ports and an IP allowlist.
[02:28] Kevin Li: And KMS — we have a central HSM, we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys for both model artifacts and logs.
[02:36] Marisol Chen: Short answer: yes for KMS integration in Private, and Dedicated can be configured to use customer keys depending on the package; we'll share specifics. For hosted there's an encrypted-at-rest flows but not customer-managed keys in the default tier.

[03:00] Jamie Park: Ok checklist items: 1) Access: service account + IP allowlist + SSO provisioning; 2) Benchmark harness: tokenization, sample workload, endpoint config; 3) Milestones: kickoff, access complete, mid-point review, final exec readout. Proposed timeline: 4 week POC. Kickoff now, access by EOW (this Friday), first bench run next week, mid-point in two weeks, exec readout week 4. Thoughts?
[03:27] Dana Price: Four weeks sounds fine. We need a 1 pager for the exec readout that maps business impact — e.g., estimated cost savings and latency improvement versus current infra.

[03:45] Marisol Chen: We'll produce that readout template. For benchmarks, suggested metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, cost per 1k tokens, error rate, percent degraded responses. We'll also capture quality metrics — a small eval set for correctness/regression.

[04:08] Ravi Patil: For quality, we'll provide 200 prompt/response pairs and a rubric. We'll need to know what models you'll use in the POC and whether you can swap quantized variants to test cost/latency tradeoffs.

[04:22] Marisol Chen: We'll propose 3 model variants: open baseline (e.g., Llama family), optimized quantized fast path, and Redwood-verified higher quality variant. We can do automatic fallback in the serving runtime and log differences.

[04:40] Elsa Moreno: About load sizing — our expectation is peak 120 QPS with average 25 QPS, but bursts up to 300 QPS for short windows. Can Redwood simulate burst behavior?
[04:52] Marisol Chen: Yes, we can run concurrency tests and synthetic traffic. For realistic cache/KV behavior we recommend a warmup phase so prefix caching hits reflect production. If your workload is reranking-heavy, we need to model that separately because it impacts GPU memory differently.

[05:14] Kevin Li: On security again — do you provide audit logs and the ability to store them into our SIEM? Also retention controls per tenant?
[05:22] Omar Reyes: We do provide audit logging; retention tiers are configurable in Dedicated and Private. We'll include the security pack — SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration docs in the repo.

[05:40] Jamie Park: I'll upload the security pack after the call. (link: https://redwood.ai/security-pack/CRM-87341)

[06:05] Ravi Patil: Back to milestones — what does "access complete" mean exactly? Service account with perms? Test VPC peering?
[06:13] Marisol Chen: Access complete = service account with token, read-only S3 (or equivalent) access for test data, networking rules in place, and a small smoke endpoint validated by our team. Then we'll run a short baseline job to validate instrumentation.

[06:28] Elsa Moreno: For peering we need a manifest of required CIDRs and ports and a sample terraform snippet would be ideal.
[06:34] Marisol Chen: We'll send a network manifest and terraform examples today.

[07:02] Dana Price: On the exec readout — who needs to be in the room on your side? We typically want a 30 minute slot with engineering and a 15 minute with execs.
[07:12] Jamie Park: We recommend a 45 minute readout: 25 minutes technical + metrics, 10 minutes business impact, 10 minutes Q&A. We'll bring the SE + AE and optionally a product mgr if needed.

[07:36] Ravi Patil: Can you outline what benchmark pass/fail looks like? We want a clear go/no-go for production.
[07:44] Marisol Chen: Pass criteria proposal: p95 latency <= 400ms for the 60% short + 30% medium mix under configured QPS; cost per 1k tokens within 20% of your internal target; quality regression <= 5% on our rubric. Any failure in security or no KMS integration would be an immediate non-starter.

[08:06] Kevin Li: That last bit is important — KMS and auditability are blockers. If Redwood cannot meet KMS for logs we can't proceed.
[08:14] Jamie Park: Understood — we'll confirm KMS details in the security pack.

[08:32] Ravi Patil: Bench specifics — Marisol, can you define the synthetic traffic shape you'll run and how you'll reproduce token distributions?
[08:40] Marisol Chen: We'll provide a harness that samples from your token length histogram; it supports ramp, steady, and spike profiles. We'll also include a reranking profile that hits the models multiple times per request to emulate your pipeline.

[09:02] Elsa Moreno: About data — we can't share production PII. We'll create masked datasets and a small synthetic generator for longer sequences.
[09:10] Marisol Chen: That's perfect. Masked data works; we'll document the tokenization differences if any.

[09:28] Jamie Park: Let's talk timeline concretely: Week 0 (this week) kickoff + access. Week 1 baseline benchmarks + tuning. Week 2 mid-point technical review (30-45 mins) to assess perf and any infra blockers. Week 3 tuning and second benchmark. Week 4 exec readout. Does that sequence align?
[09:46] Dana Price: Yes. We also want a health gate before week 3 to decide whether to continue to exec readout or extend the pilot.

[10:02] Marisol Chen: We'll define gate checks for week 2: if p95 latency reduction < 10% vs baseline or cost is > 25% above target, we surface remediation options and decide extension.

[10:18] Ravi Patil: Who's owning the mid-point readout from crestline? I'll be primary; Elsa will cover infra and Kevin security. Dana will join if we need exec decisions.

[10:28] Jamie Park: Great. Quick logistics: Marisol will need a service account and an engineer from your side to validate network rules during peering. Omar will coordinate scheduling.

[10:38] Omar Reyes: I'll send a scheduling poll for the mid-point review; target window two weeks from today.

[11:01] Speaker 1: (mumble) question about quantization and whether you can run 4-bit and 8-bit to see tradeoffs.
[11:08] Marisol Chen: Yep, we can run both. It changes latency and quality; we'll log and present delta per variant.

[11:30] Elsa Moreno: Any limitation on token context window? We have some prompts that can go to 4k.
[11:36] Marisol Chen: We support up to 8k in the variants we'll propose; some optimized kernels behave better at 2k, we'll show comparative numbers.

[12:00] Kevin Li: About RBAC — can we restrict endpoints per service account? We want separation between dev/test and pilot.
[12:08] Marisol Chen: Yes, RBAC scoped keys and route-level permissions available in Dedicated and Private; hosted can do API keys with limited scopes.

[12:30] Dana Price: Pricing — what's the recommended model for a POC like this? Hosted credits then path to Dedicated if we want stable latency?
[12:40] Jamie Park: Exactly: hosted for fast onboarding, dedicated for predictable throughput with reserved capacity. We'll send pricing scenarios with modeled costs based on your QPS.

[13:05] Ravi Patil: Do you have any existing benchmarks against similar financial workloads? Latency targets with 2k context?
[13:12] Marisol Chen: We have anonymized case studies; I'll include a short one that matches your token mix. Not identical but helpful for expectations.

[13:34] Jamie Park: Ok let's recap and call out owners. Action items (we'll put in CRM): Jamie — security pack and pricing by 4/21; Marisol — benchmark harness + network manifest by 4/22; Elsa — provision networking and service account by 4/23; Kevin — confirm KMS integration questions by 4/21; Ravi — share rubric and 200 eval prompts by 4/23.

[14:10] Dana Price: Sounds good. One more ask — can you draft the exec one-pager with predicted cost/latency delta for our CFO?
[14:18] Jamie Park: Yes. We'll draft it after the baseline run, but we'll provide an initial modeled one-pager by 4/24.

[14:35] Ravi Patil: If we hit the gates early, can we compress the timeline?
[14:40] Marisol Chen: If access is ready and the first benchmark looks promising we can move mid-point earlier by a few days. We'll be flexible.

[15:00] Elsa Moreno: Any additional compliance docs we should expect? Dataflow diagrams, incident response?
[15:07] Omar Reyes: We'll include dataflow + incident playbook in the security pack.

[15:26] Speaker 2: (brief cross talk)

[15:35] Jamie Park: Anything else from Crestline?
[15:38] Kevin Li: Just to emphasize KMS — must be clear.
[15:41] Ravi Patil: No, that's it.

[15:54] Jamie Park: All right, thanks everyone. We'll upload the checklist and security pack and follow up with the scheduling poll. Expect the network manifest and benchmark harness link in the next 48 hours.

[16:08] Marisol Chen: I'll kick off the repo and ping Elsa for creds.

[16:15] Omar Reyes: Poll for mid-point will go out today.

[16:22] Dana Price: Thanks all.

[16:28] Jamie Park: Talk soon — meeting adjourned.

Post-call notes:
- Links shared in chat: POC checklist (internal), security pack (https://redwood.ai/security-pack/CRM-87341), benchmark harness repo (to be created).
- Risk: KMS integration is a potential hard blocker; recommend priority clarifying with engineering.
- Gate criteria drafted; Marisol will circulate a formal gate doc before week 2.

End of transcript.
